requirement: A tool MUST also accept `node` and `data` together. Look up the existing ID and compare its stored identity with the deserialized `data` using `D::NodeData` equality. Use that ID on a match. An unassigned ID, malformed data, or a mismatch produces a tool error, even if the supplied data would be valid on its own. A `path` address may include `location` and must be used separately from `node` and `data`.
rationale: In `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/project_sources.rs#mod[tests]/fn[agent_node_addresses_round_trip_and_reject_inconsistent_identities_before_reads]` (or a new test marked `{test}` for `requirements.sdk.graph.validation-context.node_reference.consistency`), add a positive case that passes `node` and `data` together with a matching identity, for example `json!({"node":entry["node"],"data":entry["data"]})`. Also pass a node ID and matching data for a child, such as the `impl[Parser]/fn[parse]` node with its data string. Assert that the read succeeds and that its text and dependencies equal those from the node-only and data-only reads. — The requirement says a tool MUST accept `node` and `data` together, and MUST use the existing ID when the stored identity equals the data. The test covers only the rejections: mismatched data, unassigned ID with valid data, malformed data with a valid node, and path combined with node or data. Its successful reads use `node` alone, `data` alone, or `path` alone. The child object passed to `read_node` has `node`, `file`, `selector` and `header`, but no `data`. A search of the crates found no other test that makes a successful read with both `node` and `data`. An implementation that rejects every `node`+`data` request, or that ignores a matching pair, would pass all the current assertions.
